Title: Efforts under way to keep pregnant 12-year-old in school
Article:
KUCHING: The Social Welfare Department is working with the family of a pregnant 12-year-old schoolgirl to find a way for her to continue her education.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the department would discuss the matter with the girl's family and school to determine how she could continue her studies, taking into account her health and ability.
"We will discuss the matter with the family first. If possible, we do not want this child to be prevented from attending school.
"However, we need to take her condition into account, and there may be matters that need to be discussed with the family and school," she said after attending the closing ceremony of SPA @ Mind Games 2026.
Nancy said the department would also assess the need for welfare support and psychosocial services for the girl and her family to help them cope with the situation.
The department would also discuss arrangements for the baby's care after birth with the family, subject to the relevant processes and the court's considerations.
A 28-year-old
Indonesian man
was arrested in Kabong following a police report lodged by the school to assist investigations.

Title: Cobra surprises eatery operator in flood-hit kitchen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A restaurant operator experienced an unexpected scare when a cobra appeared in his flooded kitchen.
Recounting the tense moment, Muhammad Shazlly Sulaiman, 34, said the incident occurred while he and his workers were tending to the inundated kitchen before the venomous reptile emerged.
The trader at Jalan Balai Raya, Kampung Bukit Hijau, Jeram, said he had been worried about other venomous creatures like centipedes entering his shop, but had to take the risk and operate as usual.
"I never imagined a cobra would enter due to the stagnant floodwaters since I started operating here nearly a year ago.
"This area consists mostly of eateries, so when floods strike, it indirectly affects business.
"Customers are forced to turn back because they do not want to wade through the stagnant water. What is more worrying is that the weather changes every day, and we fear continuous rain will delay the floodwaters from receding," he said.
Shazlly did not deny that the drainage system near his shop was poorly maintained and said he had already lodged complaints with the authorities.
He said this was not the first time the area had been hit by stagnant floods, noting that the problem had persisted since 2021, and despite lodging complaints with fellow traders, no action had been taken.
He expressed hope that the drain in front of his shop would be cleared or deepened immediately so customers could visit without having to wade through floodwaters.
Meanwhile, a resident who wished to be known only as Ayu, 40, urged the authorities to resolve the stagnant flood issue promptly.
She said that having lived in the village for over 10 years, she had seen the water take a long time to recede, resulting in an unpleasant stench.

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: PH leads in four seats
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is leading in four seats in the Melaka election as of 7pm, according to unofficial vote counts.
The four seats are Ayer Keroh, Kesidang, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir.
In Ayer Keroh, PH candidate Kerk Chee Yee is leading with 1,450 votes, ahead of Perikatan Nasional's Datuk Seri Michael Gan, who has secured 420 votes.
Bersama's Muhaimin Lau has received 55 votes, while Bersatu's Mohd Hamnaim has 54 votes.
In Kesidang, PH's Allex Seah Shoo Chin is leading with 1225 votes, followed by PN's Albert Kok with 303 votes and Bersama's Dr Bryan Kek with 99 votes.
Meanwhile, PH's Low Chee Leong is maintaining a comfortable lead in Kota Laksamana with 2,240 votes, ahead of Barisan Nasional's Melvin Chua with 529 votes and Bersama's Ethan Lim Zhi Hao with 220 votes.
In Bandar Hilir, PH candidate Leng Chau Yen has garnered 1,703 votes, compared with BN's Jasmine Lok, who has 385 votes, and Bersama's Dr Rashidi Jalil with 128 votes.

Title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12
Article:
PONNAGYUN: A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday.
Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of the state capital, Sittwe.
"All I saw was their bodies scattered in pain. I could not find words to describe it. And we were lost with crying," she said.
"It has broken our family. There were no others except my family. We did not hear the sound of the fighter jet – it just came and dropped the bombs."
Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions that have long held sway in the nation's fringes.
The western coastal state of Rakhine is among the regions worst hit by the war. Controlled almost entirely by the ethnic minority Arakan Army (AA), it has been blockaded by the military and pummelled with regular airstrikes.
It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the latest attack.
Chit Su Wai said 12 people died in Friday's attack, a toll confirmed by Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, a rescue and emergency service.
Khine Hein Htet said a five-year-old was among the dead, while 18 others were injured in the camp, where many residents had been living for four years.
"They believed the camp was safe, and they sheltered there together. When we arrived at the scene, most of the victims had died in one place," the 24-year-old said.
He said it was not a combat area, adding: "We never thought this camp would be targeted."
Collapsed houses
The village was a mess of collapsed bamboo houses on Saturday, with the wreckage of an upturned vehicle mixed among the debris of household goods and clothes.
Locals had already removed the bodies, wrapping them in yellow and red plastic and burying them in makeshift graves.
Aung Kyaw Min, a 45-year-old tuk-tuk driver, described how he rushed to the village where his brother and sister lived after hearing of the attack.
"My sister's body was already headless while my brother was lying dead," he said, crying.
The next day, he discovered his mother had also been killed, while other relatives, including a 10-year-old, were missing.
His sister was a seamstress who took care of their mother. His brother was a tuk-tuk driver like him.
"Now all of them – my sister, brother, including my mother – were all killed. My niece and nephews are still missing, I don't know where to find them," he said.
The ACLED monitor estimates that more than 100,000 people have been killed on all sides in Myanmar since the civil war began.

Title: At the Supreme Court, Trump aims to cut the power of judges again
Article:
NEW YORK: When President Donald Trump's administration convinced the US Supreme Court last year to restrict the ability of federal judges to block his actions nationwide — a major boost to his power — the ruling left untouched a separate tool that some judges have used to stymie presidential policies.
Now Trump is taking aim at that tool as well in another challenge to judicial authority that could further insulate his far-reaching agenda against broad legal attacks.
An appeal filed by Trump's Justice Department, now pending before the Supreme Court, urges the justices to curtail the longstanding ability of judges to halt the actions of federal agencies that hold immense power to carry out the Republican president's policy priorities.
According to the administration, courts should not be able to shut down an agency's regulation entirely, instead limiting any relief granted only to the specific plaintiffs in a given case.
Aditya Bamzai, a University of Virginia expert in administrative law, said a win for Trump in the case could let the US government continue to enforce rules broadly on all but the plaintiffs in a given case, potentially for years as litigation plays out, even after judges have deemed them unlawful.
Siding with Trump "would give more flexibility to the executive branch", Bamzai said.
"Whether you like or dislike that flexibility can perhaps depend on whether you like or dislike a particular administration's policies," Bamzai added.
Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump and his allies have castigated judges who have impeded his policies — deriding some as radical or corrupt — even as he tests the limits of presidential powers.
At the Trump administration's behest, the Supreme Court in June 2025 clamped down on nationwide — or "universal" — injunctions that can block the government from enforcing a policy against anyone, not just the challengers who sued. Judges had increasingly deployed these orders in a wide array of cases against Trump, including those alleging violations of the US Constitution.
Impeding executive action
The new appeal arises from a challenge by Texas medical providers to federal rules implementing a statute Trump signed into law during his first term in office to limit unexpected medical bills. The appeal forms part of the administration's concerted push to make it harder for the judiciary to impede executive actions. The Supreme Court is expected to consider whether to take up the case early next year.
The kinds of lawsuits targeted by Trump's administration are brought under a 1946 US law called the Administrative Procedure Act, or APA, which governs the way federal agencies operate, including how regulations are implemented.
Judges and appeals courts have long claimed the power under this statute to "hold unlawful and set aside" agency regulations they deem illegal, invalidating them on a universal basis.
Since Trump returned to office, his administration has faced hundreds of lawsuits challenging his aggressive moves to limit immigration, pursue mass deportation, end diversity initiatives and curtail transgender rights, among other actions, that have pushed the boundaries of presidential authority.
Various plaintiffs have sued by invoking the APA in numerous cases, including to fight the termination of humanitarian legal status for hundreds of thousands of migrants living in the United States, major cuts to research grants related to racial minorities or LGBT people, and the use of a mass voter verification system to conduct sweeping citizenship checks.
Executive overreach
Proponents, including numerous state governments that regularly sue the federal government, say this judicial tool is an essential bulwark against executive overreach. Others say the APA is important to maintain uniform regulations applied equally to everyone.
"When an agency adopts a rule that has been held to be unlawful, sometimes the only sensible solution is to wipe it off the books," said law professor Ronald Levin of Washington University in St. Louis.
"You can't have a food-safety rule that applies only to some. You can't have an auto-safety manufacturing rule that applies only to some manufacturers," Levin said. "It's a tool they (judges) should have — not one they should use in every case, but ... there are some cases where the need for it is compelling."
The court's 2025 ruling restricting the power of judges came in litigation over Trump's bid to limit birthright citizenship, a right long recognised in the United States. That ruling addressed judicial power, not the legality of Trump's birthright citizenship directive.
Though Democratic President Joe Biden's administration had also asked the Supreme Court to rein in universal injunctions as lower courts hindered many of his key initiatives, the 2025 ruling proved to be a major victory for Trump.
The justices issued a separate 6-3 ruling last June on the legality of Trump's birthright citizenship policy, rejecting it as unconstitutional.
'Surprise medical bills'
The administration wants to extend the constraints that the Supreme Court's 2025 ruling placed on injunctions to similar orders judges may issue to invalidate policies under the APA.
The regulation at issue in the case being appealed by the administration sought to constrain "surprise" medical bills from hospitals and health providers outside a patient's health insurance network. A Texas association of medical doctors, air-ambulance providers and other plaintiffs argued that the regulation violated the APA and artificially deflated their insurance reimbursement rates.
The New Orleans-based 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals voided parts of the rule nationwide in August on the grounds of an APA violation.
The Trump administration's appeal is not challenging the 5th Circuit's decision about the regulation's legality. Rather, it seeks to prevent the judicial use of the APA to stop a policy nationwide.
The administration contends, as it did in its case against universal injunctions, that the APA does not grant courts such sweeping authority, instead allowing them to block a regulation's enforcement at most against the specific plaintiffs who challenged it in a particular case.
The Supreme Court "should return the lower courts to their proper role under the APA", the Justice Department said in its filing.
If the Supreme Court agrees, Levin said, "it would take longer for challengers to get unlawful regulations removed from the books".
Biden's administration also tried in 2023 to convince the Supreme Court to limit the use of this power by judges in a case in which Republican attorneys general from Texas and Louisiana challenged an immigration policy.
The justices did not take up the invitation and backed Biden in that case on other grounds.
Trump's administration may face pushback from a broad array of opponents on its new effort.
Texas, Florida and some other states, mostly Republican-led, had urged the 5th Circuit not to "neuter" the APA's effectiveness, calling the law important for maintaining the balance of power between states and the federal government.
"The APA is a critical tool ... to curb federal overreach and incursions into state sovereignty by executive-branch agencies," these states said.

Title: Sarawak seeks to become technology creator in AI-driven economy
Article:
SIBU: Sarawak wants to develop its own technology and innovators as it accelerates its transition to an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven, knowledge-based economy.
Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said developing homegrown technological capabilities was crucial to ensuring Sarawakians did not merely benefit from digital advances but also played a leading role in shaping future industries.
He said achieving this ambition required a highly skilled workforce, particularly engineers, researchers, data scientists, software developers and cybersecurity specialists who could develop and manage emerging technologies.
"We do not want to be the consumers of technology, but we want to be creators of technology," he said at the 11th convocation ceremony of the University of Technology Sarawak.
Abang Johari said growing international investor confidence in Sarawak's economic development model reflected the state's potential to emerge as a regional hub for advanced technologies, including AI and quantum computing.
He cited a meeting last month with SoftBank Group chairman and chief executive officer Masayoshi Son, who expressed strong interest in Sarawak's economic development model, particularly its commitment to providing free tertiary education.
Abang Johari said the state government had introduced its Free Tertiary Education Scheme this year to remove financial barriers that could prevent capable young Sarawakians, particularly those from rural and lower-income families, from pursuing higher education.
The initiative formed part of the state's long-term investment in human capital to support its economic transformation and ensure development opportunities were accessible to all Sarawakians. -- BERNAMA

Title: Melaka polls: 70.59pc of ordinary voters cast their ballots
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 70.59 per cent of ordinary voters cast their ballots in the Melaka election.
According to the Election Commission's (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring (VTO) dashboard, 472,397 voters had cast their ballots by the time polling ended at about 6pm today.
Of the 28 state constituencies, Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest voter turnout at 57.7 per cent.
The EC had set a voter turnout target of 70 per cent for the 16th Melaka election. However, the commission has yet to issue an official statement on the overall voter turnout for the polls.
In the 2021 state election, voter turnout stood at 65.85 per cent.

Title: 'Tapirs also have the right to live': Dead tapir found in Ijok
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: A tapir believed to have drowned has been found at an oil palm plantation in flood-hit Block C, Ijok.
The incident was shared by Ijok state assemblyman Jefri Mejan in a Facebook post today.
Jefri said a friend, identified as Andong, had sent him photographs of the animal while harvesting oil palm fruit at his plantation.
"He was saddened not only by the tapir's death, but also by the theft of the oil palm fruit he had worked to harvest.
"The floodwaters have yet to recede, wildlife has become a victim, and produce from the plantation is being stolen," he said.
Jefri's post also drew expressions of sympathy from social media users, with some highlighting the plight of wildlife affected by natural disasters.
He hoped a solution would be found soon to address the prolonged flooding in the area and prevent similar incidents.
"Tapirs also have the right to live," he said.
The Malayan tapir, also known as tenuk or cipan, is an endangered species native to Southeast Asia. Recognisable by its distinctive black-and-white markings, it inhabits tropical forests and plays an important role in forest regeneration by dispersing seeds.
Its survival is threatened by habitat loss, forest fragmentation and road accidents. Malaysia is estimated to have only 700 to 800 Malayan tapirs remaining in their natural habitats, according to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shuhaily remains in MCBA post pending further instructions, says IGP
Article:
AYER KEROH: Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain is continuing in his post pending further instructions, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said.
Khalid said he had yet to receive any directive on whether Shuhaily would be returned to the police.
He said Shuhaily, a police officer, was serving a two-year contract as MCBA director-general following his appointment by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"So far, I have not received any instructions regarding the matter.
"As I explained previously, Shuhaily is a police officer serving a two-year contract as MCBA director-general. His appointment was made by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"As such, I am awaiting further instructions should he be returned to the police. So far, no such instructions have been issued," he said at a press conference after visiting the polling centre at SK Tun Syed Syed Ahmad Shahabudin in Ayer Keroh today.
Asked whether Shuhaily would be suspended from duty if he returned to the force, Mohd Khalid said the police would follow the standard operating procedures (SOP) set by the Public Service Department.
"No action has been taken. I am still waiting. Once he is returned to me, I will follow the SOP set by the Public Service Department," he said.
Shuhaily was charged at the magistrate's court in Sepang, Selangor on Oct 21 with two counts of causing hurt to two police personnel.
Meanwhile, Khalid said the police personnel whose hand was severed in a parang attack while on duty in Kepong recently remained in stable condition and was still receiving treatment.
He said the case was still under investigation.
"I believe the situation may have been unexpected. Such incidents can happen, but every police officer, police personnel and member of the public has the right to defend themselves," he said.

Article:

The data showed that the 70.23 per cent figure covered only ordinary voters and excluded early and postal votes.

Title: Malaysia must move beyond manufacturing and build its own brands
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must move beyond its role in the global supply chain and become a creator and owner of intellectual property, technology and brands.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said design was a key driver in strengthening the country's industrial capabilities.
"It must be integrated throughout the entire value chain, from the initial stages of product development to commercialisation, in line with the aspirations of the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the 13th Malaysia Plan  (13MP)," he said.
His opening remarks at the Kuala Lumpur Design Summit 2026 were delivered by Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) Services Sector Development Division senior director Muhammad Zulhilmi Ahmad.
Sim said the increasingly competitive global landscape required Malaysia to move away from cost-based competition towards developing high-value products, making design an economic necessity.
"We need designs that translate into productivity, successful commercialisation and a stronger Malaysian brand capable of standing confidently in the international market," he said.
He said the creative economy could also generate greater added value for the country's industrial sector, particularly in the digital era.
The sector not only creates jobs and generates income but also supports entrepreneurs and creative practitioners, including designers, artists and community-based businesses.
Malaysia's
cultural and creative industry
contributed RM130.7 billion, or 6.8 per cent of gross domestic product, in 2024, up 7.1 per cent from the previous year. Exports of creative products reached RM63 billion.
"Malaysia possesses talent, a robust industrial sector and a holistic policy framework. What we need now is to bring all these strengths together to connect the dots and transform potential into shared prosperity," he said.
The creative economy, also known as the orange economy, has been identified as a priority area for future growth under the 13MP and the Asean Socio-Cultural Community pillar.
MITI, in collaboration with the Malaysia Design Council, is also part of a pioneer group working to establish the Asean Centre of Excellence for Creative Industries.
The centre will be set up in Manila, the Philippines, in conjunction with the Philippines' Asean chairmanship in 2026. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US proposed ceding Ukrainian territory in exchange for joining Nato: Zelenskyy
Article:
KYIV: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States proposed that Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for joining Nato, and that his government was in talks on "specific" security guarantees from the West.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelenskyy told reporters on Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday.
He said Ukraine was discussing "specific security guarantees from Nato and the EU" and that if Western countries confirmed them, "then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own."

Title: Saifuddin: Home Ministry only implements house arrest decisions
Article:
LUMUT: The Home Ministry is responsible for implementing decisions on house arrest but does not decide on pardon petitions or determine eligibility.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, said pardon petitions submitted by prisoners fell under the jurisdiction of the Pardons Board, which was responsible for discussing, considering and deciding on them.
"Regardless of who they are, whether ordinary people or prominent figures, rich or poor, VIPs or members of the public, everyone has the right to submit a pardon petition under the law.
"Whether a petition is submitted, discussed, considered or decided upon does not fall within the Home Ministry's area of responsibility.
"If a decision is made, our duty is to implement it, whether the sentence is reduced, cancelled, the prisoner is released or placed under house arrest," he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating the handover ceremony for the Madani Adopted Village and Adopted School programmes by the Malaysian Volunteer Department (Rela) in Kampung Sungai Tiram, Lekir, Sitiawan.
Also present were Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman and Rela director-general Datuk Rosli Yaakub.
Saifuddin said the right to submit a pardon petition was not a privilege reserved for VIPs or high-profile individuals, but was available to all prisoners entitled to do so under the law.
He said anyone convicted after going through the legal process had the right to submit a petition while serving their sentence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Panther trapped after raiding durian orchard in Jelebu
Article:
JELEBU: A male adult black panther weighing about 27kg was captured in Kampung Purun this morning, after a nearly three-week wait.
He was caught in a trap set up by the Negri Sembilan Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) around 7am.
State Perhilitan director Wan Mat Wan Harun said the department received a report on July 8 about the animal's presence at a durian orchard.
He said the complainant suspected the black panther had preyed on chickens kept at the orchard.
"Perhilitan then set up a trap on Oct 27 to capture the animal. The adult male black panther is estimated to be between three and four years old," he told reporters.
Wan Mat said veterinary officers found the animal to be in good health, with no serious injuries.
He said it would be released into a protected area under Perhilitan's supervision.
Asked whether more black panthers could be roaming the area, Wan Mat said this was possible, as the captured animal was still young.
He added that the trap would remain operational.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,787 flood victims remain at relief centres in 3 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,787 flood victims from 480 families are still taking shelter at 12 temporary relief centres (PPS) in three states as at 5pm today.
According to the Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal, the affected states are Selangor, Perak and Sarawak.
Selangor recorded the highest number, with 1,531 victims from 410 families taking shelter at eight PPS in the Kuala Selangor district.
In Perak, 220 victims from 64 families are staying at two PPS in the Hilir Perak district.
In Sarawak, 36 victims from six families remain at two PPS in the Kuching and Miri districts.
Of the total number of victims, 1,101 are adults, including 135 senior citizens, while 635 are children and 51 are babies.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in nine states and federal territories until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Kedah (Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, Sik, Pendang, Kuala Muda, Yan and Kota Setar), Penang and Perak (Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah and Manjung).
The same conditions are forecast in Selangor (Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor and Gombak), Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Negri Sembilan (Port Dickson).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Miri (Marudi), Bintulu, Sibu (Selangau), Mukah (Dalat and Matu), Sri Aman (Sri Aman and Pantu) and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Membakut), Tawau (Kalabakan and Tawau) and the West Coast (Papar).
"Thunderstorm warnings are short-term alerts valid for no more than six hours for each issuance," MetMalaysia said.

Title: Shafie: Borneo Bloc must deliver concrete action for Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The formation of the Borneo Bloc will mean little if the voices and interests of Sabahans are not heard and their demands are not translated into concrete action.
Warisan president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal said efforts to unite the voices of Sabahans should go beyond political cooperation.
He said unity must be followed by action to realise the state's rights and interests.
Shafie said decades of voicing Sabah's demands would bring little change if outstanding issues continued to be delayed without resolution.
These included the state's claim to a 40 per cent special grant from federal revenue, which is still subject to an appeal.
"There is no point in speaking up for decades if we do not act on what we have called for.
"Today, the announcement on the 40 per cent claim is still under appeal and has been delayed again. So, where do we go from here?
"There is no point in uniting Sabah's voice if our actions go in different directions," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference at Warisan headquarters.
On the possibility of political cooperation through the Borneo Bloc, Shafie said Warisan was still examining possible forms of cooperation with certain parties to strengthen Sabah's interests and its ability to pursue its demands.
He said political unity in Sabah must have a clear direction and should not depend solely on alliances between parties at the national level.
Shafie said elected representatives from national parties operating in Sabah should also be assessed on their ability to champion the state's interests, rather than simply follow the positions taken by their respective party presidents.
In March, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor dismissed claims that efforts were underway to form a "Borneo Bloc".
He said Sabah and Sarawak remained part of Malaysia and should work with the federal government to strengthen the nation.
"We are one country, and there must be cooperation between all parties — the states and the federal government — to further strengthen Malaysia," he said.

Title: Ramanan: RM1mil in aid for 1,500 flood-hit families in Sg Buloh
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: Almost RM1 million in aid has been distributed to 1,500 families affected by floods in seven areas around Sungai Buloh under the Santuni Madani Kasih programme.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the assistance was provided through a collaboration between his ministry and the Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) as part of a corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative.
He said the aid comprised household essentials, including electrical appliances worth RM625 for each affected family.
"The recipients are residents of Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Kubu Gajah, Kampung Paya Jaras Hilir, Kampung Merbau Sempak, Kampung Sungai Pelong and Kampung Paya Jaras Tengah.
"While the assistance is small compared with the huge losses suffered by flood victims, we hope it will ease their burden and help them rebuild their lives after enduring 16 consecutive days of flooding," he told the media at the Santuni Madani Kasih programme at Dewan Astana Era Mewah today.
Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohamed Shamir Abd Aziz.
Ramanan, who is also Sungai Buloh member of parliament, said he would instruct officers to ensure that all the aid reached the flood victims.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also announced an additional special cash aid of RM2,500 for each eligible head of household affected by the floods in Selangor to help ease their financial burden.
"The state government has also provided RM500 in aid to victims who registered at temporary relief centres.
"A temporary retention pond worth RM12 million will be built in Sungai Buloh to reduce the flash floods that frequently affect the area," he said.

Title: Food security a national development priority - Fadillah
Article:
KUCHING: Food security is not merely an agricultural concern but a national development priority closely connected to household well-being, economic resilience and community stability.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said global developments had highlighted how vulnerable food supply chains can be to external disruptions, rising production costs and climate-related challenges.
"We must therefore continue strengthening domestic food production while building more resilient and sustainable food systems.
"In Sarawak, we are blessed with considerable potential - our land resources, agricultural diversity, rich biodiversity and the knowledge of our local communities. Our responsibility is to ensure that these strengths translate into productive opportunities and sustainable livelihoods," he said.
Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation minister, said this in his speech at the RISE 2026: Rising Impact Through Sustainable Empowerment programme.
Fadillah said community-led food security initiatives were particularly valuable as they cultivated not only crops but also knowledge, cooperation, self-reliance and a greater sense of ownership.
"When communities learn to produce, manage and sustain their own food resources, they are not only improving their immediate well-being.
"They are building resilience against future uncertainties," he said.

Title: Police have investigated suspected AI chip transshipment since April 2025, says Saifuddin
Article:
LUMUT: Police have been investigating allegations that Malaysia was used as a transit hub for the re-export of high-tech artificial intelligence (AI) chips since April 2025, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the investigation was conducted under the Strategic Trade Act, with the police also serving on the Strategic Trade Action Committee (STAC) under the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti).
Saifuddin said any new findings from the police investigation were relayed to Miti, which is the lead agency, as the complaint over the alleged AI chip exports was raised by the United States government with the ministry.
However, he described the investigation as highly complex, involving multiple layers of inquiry and several agencies represented in STAC.
"Police opened an investigation paper as early as April 2025. If there are any findings, we will update Miti, and it is the ministry's responsibility to relay them to the party that lodged the complaint.
"Our (police) investigation is focused on whether Malaysia was used as a transit hub. So, to answer whether the police are investigating the matter, the answer is yes. We began our investigation as soon as the allegations emerged.
"Whether the findings establish evidence to support the allegations of diversion or illegal procurement involves multiple layers of investigation, making it a highly complex matter," he told reporters.
Saifuddin was speaking after officiating the People's Volunteer Corps (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani handover ceremony at Kampung Sungai Tiram, Lekir, Sitiawan.
He said STAC comprised several agencies besides the police, including Bank Negara Malaysia, the Inland Revenue Board, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission and the Customs Department.
Yesterday,
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim
said the government has yet to find any indication linking Nvidia AI chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd and their subsequent re-export from Malaysia to other countries.
The issue involves Singapore-based Megaspeed International and its Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd.
This followed an earlier statement by Miti that it had
not granted any approvals
to either company.
Miti said Speedmatrix was a tenant at a data centre in Malaysia, adding that any verification visits to the facility were part of the ministry's routine monitoring of the data centre sector and should not be interpreted as an indication that a company was facing difficulties obtaining approval.
The ministry said any claims to the contrary were inaccurate.

Title: As smog hangs over Lahore, Pakistan's new pollution squad races to douse stubble fires
Article:
LAHORE: As smog again settles over large parts of South Asia, Pakistani authorities are widening a crackdown on illegal stubble burning, which they say is fuelling the region's annual pollution crisis.
On Thursday, officers of a new quick-response unit stepped out of their vehicles at a paddy field on the edge of Lahore.
Smoke curled low over the stubble, and the crew had the fire under control within minutes, preventing it from adding to the haze over a city that Swiss group IQAir rated "very unhealthy" earlier this week.
Farmers in the region commonly set leftover rice residue alight after the October harvest, fuelling a toxic mix of industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust and construction dust that lingers under cold winter air, driving pollution to hazardous levels.
The unit is the first of its kind in Pakistan dedicated to fighting pollution, officials say, and it is one of the most visible steps in a campaign that Punjab officials claim is working.
Satellites have detected less burned area in India and Pakistan than the historical average at this point in the year, even as many locals in Pakistan say they struggle to notice improvements.
Carrot and stick approach
Silwat Saeed, chief of the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department in Pakistan's Punjab, said the government this year formed a 750-member force in 67 rapid-response units across major rice-growing districts.
Teams aim to reach reported field fires within 10 to 15 minutes. Officials also patrol paddy areas for signs of burning, while complaints can be lodged locally, said Ashfaq Hussain, a deputy director of the force.
"We receive complaints through multiple channels and respond to them in the shortest possible time," he said.
[[nid:1577544]]
In a single 24-hour period this week, the department received 679 field fire reports from across Punjab and said it extinguished 650 of them.
Violators face fines, arrest or both. Farmers caught burning stubble face fines of 15,000 Pakistani rupees (US$54) per acre, said Muhammad Farooq, an assistant director of the Punjab Agriculture Department. Those who fail to pay the fines can also face prosecution and a possible jail term of up to six months.
The government has also distributed more than 10,000 subsidised super seeders, paying 60 per cent of their cost while farmers pay the remaining 40 per cent.
Ongoing health crisis
Muhammad Ismail, who farms 50 acres, said switching from stubble burning to a subsidised super seeder and other machinery had significantly boosted his wheat yield per acre.
Yet adoption is far from universal. Saleem Abbas, another local farmer who has shifted away from stubble burning, said many still favour the practice because it is widely regarded as the cheapest and fastest way to clear fields for the next crop.
Over recent years, Pakistan and India have each accused the other of worsening the air. Saeed said the challenge is huge for both countries and that Pakistan has raised it with Indian officials at international forums.
India's foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
In recent days, patients have crowded benches and corridors at local hospitals in Lahore. Abdullah Nayyar, director-general of the Punjab Environment Protection Department, said health department data show smog-related throat hospitalisations last month were only at 69 per cent of the level recorded in October 2025.
But at Lahore's Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Ahmed Abubakar, a heart patient who has had a bypass and is diabetic, said smog had brought on breathing problems and eye infections.
Mohammad Niaz Butt, who said his nose and throat blocked up, put it bluntly: "They are burning it, and nothing is done about it."

Title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak-level Deepavali celebration
Article:
IPOH: Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah and Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim attended the Perak-level Deepavali celebration at Stadium Indera Mulia.
Raja Muda of Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa and Raja Di Hilir of Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah also attended the event.
Their Royal Highnesses arrived about 2.30pm and were received by Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and state Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A Sivanesan, along with 15,000 visitors from various ethnic communities.
At the event, Sultan Nazrin also presented cash contributions to 69 orphans from six care centres and welfare organisations.
Meanwhile, Saarani said in his speech that no matter how remarkable human intellectual achievements or how advanced civilisation became, people would always need love to show compassion, empathy to understand others, and wisdom to appreciate them.
"For progress may transform the face of the world, but it is nobility of character that shapes the face of humanity," he said.
He said Perak's own history showed how people of various ethnic backgrounds had worked together, contributing their energy, efforts and wisdom to build the state's prosperity.
He said the history of Perak would be incomplete without recognising the early Indian community's contributions in clearing plantations and building railway lines, roads and ports despite great hardship.
Saarani said the Indian community's heritage in Perak was also reflected in education, culture and religion.
He said the existence of 134 Tamil National-Type Schools - the highest number in the country - reflected a long history of efforts to strengthen education for younger generations.
Likewise, places of worship that had stood for generations formed part of the state's historical heritage and cultural diversity, enriching its identity.

Title: Thunderstorms and heavy rain in 7 states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather affects Penang and Kedah in Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, Sik, Pendang, Kuala Muda, Yan, and Kota Setar.
In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung.

Title: Saifuddin: No disruption to MCBA operations amid director-general's legal case
Article:
LUMUT: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency continues to carry out its duties without disruption despite the legal proceedings involving its director-general, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said issues involving the agency's top leadership should not bring the entire organisation to a standstill or affect its responsibilities.
Saifuddin said he had instructed Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman to give special attention to managing the situation, which was unprecedented.
"I assure you that MCBA operations have not been affected because the agency plays an important role in controlling and protecting the country's borders. The entire organisation cannot be allowed to stop functioning because of an issue involving its director-general.
"I am grateful that, based on reports from the ground, its operations have continued without disruption. In fact, officers have successfully foiled several attempts, including a recent case involving a couple carrying a large amount of cash into Singapore," he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating the Malaysian Volunteer Corps Department (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani handover ceremony at Kampung Sungai Tiram, Lekir, Sitiawan, today.
Asked whether the agency would receive a new director-general soon, Saifuddin said the process had not reached that stage.
"We are not there yet. Let us settle one matter at a time.
"If the matter involves court proceedings, we will allow the legal process to take its course," he said.
On Oct 29, Saifuddin announced that the Home Ministry had decided to return Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain to the police.
However, lawyer Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, who represents Shuhaily, was reported to have said that his client
remained as the director-general
as he had yet to receive an official letter or directive on the decision to return him to the police force.
Shuhaily was appointed MCBA director-general for a two-year term from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027.
On Oct 21, he pleaded not guilty at the Sepang magistrate's court to two charges of causing hurt to two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28, 2026.

Title: 'I may lose my mind': Frustrated travelers stuck in US flight havoc
Article:
NEW YORK: Confusion reigned at airports across the United States on Friday as a rare grounding of all US flights stranded hundreds of thousands of frustrated travelers.
In New York's busy LaGuardia airport, Janice Llewellyn was on the verge of tears: the chaos could mean she will miss her daughter's wedding in Toronto.
The 61-year-old Llewellyn was desperate to find an alternative route, telling AFP: "I may lose my mind."
"My husband flew all the way from England to get to the wedding," she said.
"Oh gosh! I wish they had another flight, I wish I could get another flight, like, now."
At the airport in Las Vegas, some fliers were told their journeys were delayed due to wind.
One airline staffer said the ground stop would last eight hours. Another said 24 hours.
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) officials eventually lifted the ground stop at 8:15 pm ET (0115 GMT Saturday).
"It will take us time (to) resume normal operations," Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said, blaming the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment.
During the stop, the lack of information led many passengers to form long lines at rental car counters in a mad dash for travel alternatives.
Joseph Anderson said he was trying to get back to Oakland in California from Las Vegas and was considering driving – but said "if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too."
[[nid:1577525]]
The 72-year-old retired Air Force veteran said his already-checked luggage was captive, meaning "we're kind of stuck."
"I would hope the communication can be better from the FAA," he said.
Friday 13th
The ground stop comes less than two weeks before the Thanksgiving holiday, the busiest travel period of the year in the United States.
And it falls ahead of a particularly busy weekend for professional and college sports – teams and their fans are also stuck.
Back in New York, Tiara Johnson had been heading to Orlando in Florida for a weekend concert, and any hope that she would make it was growing dim.
"You think you're gonna be there in three hours, but your whole evening is kind of done!" the 50-year-old told AFP.
"But hey, they say it's Friday the 13th!"
Harried passengers stared at their phones, calm but annoyed, wandering the airport terminal without clear direction.
Hagit Levy Shalev, 54, was zen.
She booked a new flight for Saturday morning, meaning her work trip would last a little longer.
"I'll get there," she laughed. "One more extra day away from the kids!" — AFP

Title: Asean nations sign digital economy framework agreement to deepen economic integration
Article:
MANILA: Asean nations on Saturday signed the landmark Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), a pact aimed at making it easier for businesses to trade online and reach customers across the region.
The signatories were trade ministers from all 11 Asean member states, including Malaysia's Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Philippine Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque said during the signing ceremony that the pact marked a "defining moment in Asean economic integration".
She said DEFA could help double the region's digital economy from an estimated US$1 trillion to US$2 trillion by 2030.
The agreement, she said, provides a common framework for cross-border e-commerce, electronic payments and data flows, helping businesses reach customers across the region and giving consumers greater confidence in online transactions.
"Our real task now is to translate these commitments into practical outcomes," she said.
Roque said the signing turned years of negotiations and consultations into a shared commitment to bring Asean economies closer together and widen access to the benefits of digital trade.
She said the agreement provides a common framework for cross-border e-commerce, electronic payments and data flows, helping businesses reach customers across the region and giving consumers greater confidence in online transactions.
Roque said Asean governments must work together to put the necessary infrastructure in place and ensure the agreement is implemented in a way that meets the needs of smaller businesses.
Roque urged businesses to invest in digital solutions, strengthen regional partnerships and help bring micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) into the digital economy.
DEFA negotiations concluded in May after Asean senior economic officials resolved the remaining issues at a meeting in Manila from May 27 to 29.

Title: Motorist slashed, kicked in Penang road rage attack; suspect jailed eight months
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 54-year-old motorist suffered slash wounds to his right arm and abdomen after being attacked with a knife in a road rage incident near SK Batu Lancang on Nov 4.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police detected a video of the assault circulating on social media today.
He said investigations found that the incident occurred about 2.07pm, involving the victim and a 30-year-old man.
"The victim, a 54-year-old man, sustained slash wounds to his right arm and abdomen from a knife wielded by a 30-year-oldman," he said in a statement.
Rozak said the attack stemmed from the suspect's dissatisfaction with the victim's driving.
The case was investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, an offence punishable by up to 10 years' imprisonment, a fine, whipping, or any combination of two of these punishments.
He said the suspect, Abdul Kader Aminullah, an unemployed man was arrested and charged in court on Nov 11, where he pleaded guilty and sentenced to eight months' imprisonment.
Earlier, a social media user claiming to be the victim's friend shared footage of the incident on Facebook.
The user said a motorcyclist had cut between two cars before stopping abruptly, causing the victim's car to lightly nudge the motorcycle.
They said the motorcyclist then opened the victim's car door and assaulted him with his fists and a box cutter, before kicking him in the head.
The user also said that the victim, described as soft-spoken and prone to seizures, was left traumatised by the incident despite lodging a police report.
